I didn't run `crimes scan` myself. I used the JSON you supplied and read the three components to check it against the source. I haven't edited anything, since you asked for a proposal.

## 1. The drift is real

Two findings report it, both filed against `src/components/SeatList.tsx`: **crime_00004** (`action_label_drift`) and **crime_00009** (`copy_ia_drift`). Both name the "delete" group with the aliases `archive`, `delete` and `remove`. The source matches:

| Component | Label | href |
|---|---|---|
| `UserList.tsx:7` | **Delete** user | `/users/manage` |
| `UserList.tsx:8` | **Remove** member | `/users/manage` |
| `TeamList.tsx:6` | **Archive** team | `/teams/manage` |
| `TeamList.tsx:7` | **Delete** the seat | `/seats/manage` |
| `SeatList.tsx:6` | **Remove** member | `/seats/manage` |
| `SeatList.tsx:7` | **Archive** member | `/seats/manage` |

Each file uses two of the three verbs, and each verb appears in exactly two files. That fits the evidence lines: `"archive" in 2 file(s)`, `"delete" in 2 file(s)`, `"remove" in 2 file(s)`.

## 2. Proposed canonical label set

| Verb | Use | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Delete** | The one destructive action, written as `Delete <entity>` in sentence case with no article | Canonical |
| Remove | Not used for this action | Retired |
| Archive | Not used for this action | Retired |

The changes:

| File | Current | Proposed | Finding it addresses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SeatList.tsx:6` | Remove member | Delete seat | 00004: removes one `remove` hit. 00009: one label for `/seats/manage` |
| `SeatList.tsx:7` | Archive member | (drop; duplicate of line 6) | 00004: removes one `archive` hit. 00009: two labels for one destination becomes one |
| `TeamList.tsx:6` | Archive team | Delete team | 00004: removes the last `archive` hit |
| `TeamList.tsx:7` | Delete the seat | Delete seat | 00009: style fix (drop the article). The verb is already canonical |
| `UserList.tsx:8` | Remove member | Delete user (merge with line 7) | 00004: removes the last `remove` hit |

One caution on this choice. "Archive" usually means reversible and "Remove member" usually means removing someone from a group without deleting their account. Nothing in this fixture backs either meaning: there are no handlers, and every item just links to a `/…/manage` page. So collapsing all three into "Delete" is correct here. If your real product does support restoring archived items or removing someone from a group, that is a second action and needs its own verb, documented as an exception. Even then, because `remove` and `archive` are in the detector's "delete" group, these findings will keep firing until you suppress them for that case.

## 3. Which component to refactor first: `SeatList.tsx`

- It is the file both findings are filed against.
- It contains no use of the canonical verb, so both of its labels need changing.
- It is the only file that carries both verbs being retired (`remove` and `archive`). Fixing it first cuts each of those down to one file, which leaves single edits in `TeamList` and `UserList`.
- It is the clearest case of the IA problem: two labels in the same sidebar point to the same href.

After that, do `TeamList.tsx`, which removes the last `archive`. The "Delete the seat" item is also odd: it's a seat action in the team view, which is a separate placement question. Finish with `UserList.tsx`, which removes the last `remove`.

## 4. How `action_label_drift` and `copy_ia_drift` differ on this fixture

On this fixture they hardly differ at all. Both have the same `summary`, the same five evidence lines, the same file they're filed against, the same `related_files`, the same severity (0.4) and confidence (0.6), and the same `pick_canonical_label` suggested action. The only differences are:

- **`fix_shape`**:
  - `action_label_drift` says "pick one verb per action; update labels uniformly". That's about verb vocabulary.
  - `copy_ia_drift` says "pick the canonical label; redirect copies to it". That's about UI text and navigation: several copies pointing at one place.
- **`agent_risk`**: 0.31 for `action_label_drift` and 0.29 for `copy_ia_drift`.

So both appear to use the same alias-group matcher here. I can only infer that from the output, because I haven't read the detector source. The difference in purpose shows in the source, not in the evidence. `action_label_drift` is about which verb you use. `copy_ia_drift` is about labels as navigation, and that's where `/seats/manage` matters: three labels reach it ("Delete the seat", "Remove member", "Archive member"), and the identical "Remove member" goes to two different destinations. The detector's evidence doesn't mention hrefs, so that reading is mine. That's why the table above links verb changes to 00004 and the "one label per destination" changes to 00009.

In practice, treat the two as **one fix, counted twice**. The total of 13 findings overstates this problem. A single "Delete" pass should clear both findings, which a re-scan should confirm. It would be worth having the tool merge or link these two findings when their evidence matches exactly.
